newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil inmates free hostages, end rebellion.
newsitem.headline: Brazil inmates free hostages, end rebellion.

text.p: Rioting inmates have freed their last three hostages unharmed, ending a three-day siege at a prison in southern Brazil, police said on Friday.
Military police moved in and took control of the prison in Florianopolis, capital of Santa Catarina state, after the guards were released late on Thursday night.
"All the hostages came out well," Police Col. Sergio Wallner told Reuters. "There were no physical injuries among the hostages although, mentally, they were nervous."

Some 300 prisoners seized the prison and took 10 guards hostage on Tuesday morning to complain about torture and overcrowding and demand transfers. Military police surrounded the jail, but never launched an attack to quell the riot.
To end the stand-off, authorities agreed to transfer some prisoners to other jails.
A police spokeswoman said more than 100 prisoners remained in Florianopolis State Penitentiary, which was damaged in the riot. Police have begun an investigation into the rebellion.
